CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS

CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.gov in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

11B.

During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, JUNE 12, 2025,
7:00 PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

  1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

  2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Ryan Klement, New Life Community Church.

  3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Troop 394.

  4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jennifer Hong
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Sophia M. Tse
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Lynda P. Johnson
  Mayor/Chair Frank Aurelio Yokoyama

  5.  Presentations/Appointments

  5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council honoring:

  Dr. Winston Wong (Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander Heritage
  Month).

  6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  Jarrod Lujan expressed concern regarding public safety at the property owned by the Los
  Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority, located northwest of Gridley Road
  and 183rd Street.

  Teddy Lloyd offered various suggestions for potential revenue generating opportunities,
  for the City.

  Saul Lozada expressed concern regarding the quality of workmanship on City projects at
  the Cerritos Senior Center.

  Al Barlevy thanked the City for recognizing Jewish American Heritage Month and spoke
  regarding his community outreach efforts, expressing concern regarding recent
  nationwide and global occurrences.

  Mel Cortez commended the Cerritos Sheriff’s Station for its efforts in public safety
  improvements and requested updates on City projects.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, June 12, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 18

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Sam Desai spoke regarding changes to the City’s event schedule; offered suggestions
  regarding Councilmember presence on social media; and spoke in support of
  transparency and fiscal responsibility.

  Artellia Johnson spoke regarding the importance of community representation and public
  participation in municipal government.

  Elaine Magee Magee expressed concern regarding pest control and weed abatement on
  an easement owned by Southern California Edison, located near her property.

  Gilbert Lapena expressed concern regarding public safety at the property owned by the
  Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority, located northwest of Gridley
  Road and 183rd Street.

  Howard Sachs expressed concern regarding management responsiveness at the Ivy Park
  at Cerritos facility.

  Bill Sinko, Community Family Guidance Center representative, thanked the City Council
  for its support of the nonprofit organization and shared an update on the services
  provided to the Cerritos community.

  Chris Yates, Deepa Badhwar, and Dr. Etelvina Jurado, Cerritos Chamber of Commerce
  (Chamber) representatives, shared updates related to the Chamber’s administration and
  upcoming events.

  The Mayor announced that prior to the meeting, the Council/Agency members received
  full-text, unredacted copies of the two (2) written comments submitted for Item 6
  (7B.2.), by the deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the official record.
  Requests for copies of the written comments submitted for this meeting can be made
  during regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

Business Item 9A, prior to consideration of the Consent Calendar.

7B.2. (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Johnson, to authorize
  administrative-initiated Fiscal Year (FY) 2024-25 budget amendments in accordance with
  Joint Budget Resolution No. 2024-12/CSA No. 2024-01 and the Strategic Financial Plan
  and Budget Preparation Policy (Policy 2.04) as adopted by the City Council, as follows:

  1. Account/Project: 110-364-61340 (Outside Services)
  Amount: $200,000 (Transfer)
  Justification: A budget transfer is requested in the amount of $200,000 to cover
  unanticipated costs associated with emergency and preventative infrastructure work
  on Bloomfield Avenue. During routine inspection and planning for future mainline
  improvements, it was determined that several urgent actions were necessary to
  maintain the integrity and operational reliability of the water system; and

  2. Account/Project: 110-111-53080 (Travel and Meeting)
  Amount: $5,500 (New Allocation)
  Justification: A budget amendment in the amount of $5,500 is requested to cover a
  proposed international trip by Mayor Pro Tem Johnson to the Philippines, in support of
  City Council direction to pursue a potential sister city relationship with a jurisdiction in
  the Philippines. The City Council Travel and Meeting budget is allocated to cover
  routine domestic travel by the City Council throughout the fiscal year. International
  travel is not budgeted as a component of the Travel and Meeting budget. Accordingly,
  a budget amendment in the form of a new allocation is required to accommodate the
  proposed travel. Approval of this budget amendment is in accordance with City Policy
  No. 1.12.040(c) (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 1) as follows:

  NOES:  Hong

  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING PRECISE PLAN 2025-5, A PROPOSAL BY CLARKDALE

  IS LOCATED AT 17200-17224 CLARKDALE AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA 90703
